chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Murazam who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When one of you intends something, let him pray two Rak'at, then let him praise Allah and laud Him, and let him send blessings upon Muhammad and the People of his Household, and he should say: O Allah! If this matter is good for me in my religion and my world, then make it easy for me and decree it for me; and if it is other than that, then turn it away from me.'
So I asked him: 'What should I recite in these two?' So he said: 'Recite in these two whatever you wish, and if you wish, recite in these two: Say, He is Allah, One, and Say, O you unbelievers!'

key_terms.أَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ: The People of his Household (Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say, He is Allah, One (Surah Al-Ikhlas)

ai.seo_question: What is the procedure and supplication for Salat al-Istikhara according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the foundational ritual for Salat al-Istikhara, emphasizing the integration of voluntary prayer with a supplication that seeks divine alignment of one's choice with both spiritual and worldly well-being. Scholarly tradition highlights the flexibility in recitation, allowing for any Quranic verses, while specifically recommending Surah Al-Ikhlas and Al-Kafirun for their thematic resonance with monotheism and divine choice. This practice reflects the Shia emphasis on seeking guidance through the Prophet and Ahl al-Bayt, ensuring decisions are rooted in faith rather than mere desire.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Hadeed, from Murazam who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said to me: ‘Whenever one of you intends something, so let him pray two Rak’at of Salāt, then let him Praise Allahazwj and let him Laud upon Himazwj, and let him send Blessings upon Muhammadsaww and the Peopleasws of hissaww Household, and he should be saying, ‘O Allahazwj! If this matter was good for me in my Religion, and my world, so Make it easier for me; and if it was other than that, so Exchange it from me’.

So I asked himasws, ‘Which thing should I recite in these two?’ So heasws said: ‘Recite in these two whatever you so desire to, and if you so desire to, recite in these two [112:1] Say He Allah is One (Chapter 112) and [109:1] Say: O you unbelievers! Chapter 109)’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Murazim who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said to me, ‘If one of you may think of doing something, he should perform two Rak‘at Salah (prayer), then praise Allah, speak of His greatness and say, “Allahumma Salli ‘Ala Muhammad wa ‘Ali Muhammad (O Allah grant Muhammad and his family a compensation worthy of their serving Your cause).” Thereafter say, “O Lord, if this matter is good for my religion and worldly matters, please make it possible for me with ease; and if it is otherwise, keep it away from me.’”
I then asked, ‘What should I read in the two Rak‘at Salah (prayer)?’ The Imam replied, ‘You may read whatever you like. You can read Chapter 112 or 109.’”
